title: The Sixth Sense
events_chronological: Child psychologist Malcolm Crowe and his wife Anna celebrate a civic award for his work with children.
A former patient, Vincent Grey, breaks into their bathroom, accuses Malcolm of having failed him, shoots him in the stomach and then kills himself.
Malcolm bleeds to death on the bedroom floor with Anna beside him.
The following autumn Malcolm takes on nine-year-old Cole Sear, a withdrawn boy whose case reminds him of Vincent's.
Cole's mother Lynn keeps finding cupboards standing open, drawers pulled out and marks on her son's body that she cannot explain.
Cole is shut in a cupboard at a birthday party and comes out hysterical and bruised.
Malcolm arrives late for his wedding anniversary dinner and Anna leaves the restaurant without speaking to him.
Cole finally tells Malcolm that he sees dead people walking around who do not know that they are dead.
Malcolm almost drops the case, then replays the old tape of Vincent Grey and hears a terrified voice in Spanish behind his own.
Malcolm tells Cole to stop running from the ghosts and to listen to what they want from him.
Kyra Collins, a girl who has just died, appears in Cole's tent and hands him a videotape.
At Kyra's wake Cole gives her father the tape, which shows her stepmother poisoning her food.
Cole tells his mother about the ghosts and repeats what his dead grandmother heard her say at the graveside, and Lynn believes him.
No longer terrified, Cole is cast in the school play and is happy in it.
Malcolm tells Cole that he has helped him and that the two of them will not need to see each other again.
Malcolm goes home, watches his and Anna's wedding video, and sees that she is asleep and has been talking to no one.
Anna's hand opens and Malcolm's wedding ring falls out, and he finds the bullet wound in his own back.
Malcolm tells his sleeping wife that he loves her and lets go.
syuzhet_notes: The film runs almost strictly forward, and its single displacement is the one that matters: told-order bullet 17 is a flashback to the night of the shooting, suppressed for the whole runtime and released only in the closing montage, which also replays earlier scenes to show that nobody but Cole has spoken to Malcolm since. The nonlinearity here is one withheld event rather than a shuffled timeline.
fabula_notes: Malcolm's death is elided by a caption reading "the next fall", so the months between the shooting and the Cole case are inferred rather than shown. That every scene between Malcolm and Anna is in fact a man talking to a woman who cannot hear him is established retroactively and never played as such at the time.
